headlines.title: Jury convicts man in late-night sexual assault on San Francisco Muni bus
headlines.description: San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins announced Tuesday that her office secured a conviction against 26-year-old Dasan Warsaialem Brown following a jury trial for the sexual assault of a passenger on a city bus. Brown was convicted of multiple charges, including assault with intent to commit a felony, attempted rape by force or violence or by threat of bodily injury, attempted sexual penetration by a foreign object by force and violence, sexual battery by restraint, simple assault, assault with force likely to cause great bodily injury, felony false imprisonment and two counts of misdemeanor vandalism. “I would like to thank the jury for their time and attention to the evidence in this trial,” Jenkins said. “This verdict reinforces our city’s commitment to holding those who commit acts of sexual violence accountable. We are thankful for the victim’s courage to come forward and trust in our office to obtain justice and accountability.” According to trial testimony and evidence, the attack occurred at approximately 11:40 p.m. on April 26, 2025. Brown violently assaulted the victim on the 29 Muni bus near Winston Avenue after all other passengers had disembarked. Brown attempted to rape and sexually penetrate the victim with a foreign object. During the attack, the victim was strangled, sexually assaulted and sustained injuries that included hair loss. The bus driver witnessed the assault and immediately called for help. San Francisco State University Police responded to the scene and detained Brown until San Francisco Police arrived and took him into custody. Assistant District Attorney Tanisha Gooch successfully prosecuted the case, assisted by District Attorney Investigator Shan Johnson, paralegal Andrew Ong and IT support staffer Noaeh Pinaire. The district attorney’s office issued a special thanks to victim advocates Abigail Cordova and Cindy Pelayo, who worked closely with the victim throughout the case’s pendency. Prosecutors credited the dedication of investigating officers from the San Francisco State University Police Department and the San Francisco Police Department’s Special Victims Unit and Taraval Station for helping develop a strong case. “The victim fought hard despite the odds and deserved justice in this case,” Gooch said. “I want to thank the jury for their careful consideration.” Brown is currently in custody pending sentencing, which is scheduled for Sept. 3.

headlines.title: Look up! Perseids meteor shower observable in the Bay Area this week
headlines.description: One of the calendar year’s best meteor showers will be observable as early as Tuesday night in the Bay Area, with peak showers projected to take place Wednesday night and Thursday morning, according to NASA. The Perseids are an annual meteor shower that occurs when Earth passes through a meteor stream left behind by Comet Swift-Tuttle. According to NASA, the Perseids are one of the best annual meteor showers, with 50 to 100 meteors able to be seen per hour during peak showers that leave streaks of light and color in the sky. Astrologists are also expecting this year’s Perseids to be more visible than usual due to a new moon — when the moon is dark and almost invisible in the sky — arriving on Wednesday night that will make the sky darker than normal. According to Andrew Fraknoi, a professor of astronomy at the Fromm Institute for Lifelong Learning at the University of San Francisco, the two most important factors to consider when finding a location to view meteor showers are light pollution — the amount of artificial outdoor lighting in a given area — and weather. “Find a place where the sky is clear and you can do something to get away from city lights,” said Fraknoi. “That means if you’re in your own backyard, turning off all the lights or going to a park or a woody area. Find a place where it’s dark.” According to astrologists, Bay Area residents can watch the Perseids at any location with clear weather and minimal light pollution, though many reservation-required watch party events taking place throughout the region still have tickets available. In the East Bay, Oakland’s Chabot Space and Science Center and Berkeley’s Lawrence Hall of Science, two science museums located over 1,500 feet above the Bay, will be hosting watch parties beginning Wednesday night. The Chabot Space and Science Center’s event will begin on 11 p.m. Wednesday and end at 3 a.m. Thursday, taking place on the museum’s observation deck. The event will cost $15 for adults and $7 for kids, while being free for the museum’s members. The Lawrence Hall of Science’s event will take place from 8-11 p.m. Wednesday, with general admission costing $27 for all attendees ages 3 and older, while being free for children ages 2 and under. In the North Bay, The Meritage Resort and Spa located in Napa is hosting a high-end watch party on its vineyard deck on Wednesday night. The $35 event will take place from 7:30 p.m. to midnight, with attendees receiving observational guidance from local astronomers and access to a large selection of food and beverage options. In San Francisco, there is currently no official watch parties scheduled, with Fraknoi remarking that the city is typically not the best place to watch meteor showers due to higher chances of “being overcast” due to fog or clouds. Astrologists say the meteor showers are visible without telescopes, with Fraknoi advising people against using astrological equipment to watch the showers since they “restrict” a view of the entire sky. Fraknoi also advises meteor shower watchers to be patient when looking for cosmic activity, while noting that it typically takes at least 10 to 15 minutes for peoples’ eyes to adjust to the dark so that they can see the showers.

headlines.title: Suisun City extends closure of City Hall, public services amid cybersecurity probe
headlines.description: Suisun City has extended the closure of City Hall and in-person public services through Friday, Aug. 14, as officials continue to investigate an ongoing cybersecurity incident. While internal operations are continuing, the closure affects multiple municipal divisions, including the Planning, Building, Housing, Water, Finance, Human Resources, Public Works and Administration departments, as well as the City Manager’s Office. Public safety services and emergency responses remain active despite the closures. The Suisun City police and fire departments will continue to respond to all calls for service. Furthermore, city dispatchers will continue processing 911 and non-emergency calls through the Solano County dispatch center. The Police Department lobby remains open and accessible to the public for general assistance, speaking with an officer, vehicle releases and ticket sign-offs. Lobby hours are Monday through Thursday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with a possible closure for lunch from noon to 12:30 p.m. The city is currently working alongside federal, state and regional agencies to investigate the cybersecurity incident, maintain essential services and restore its systems. Partnering agencies include the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security and the California Office of Emergency Services.

headlines.title: Air quality advisory issued as smoke from fire near Big Sur drifts into the Bay Area
headlines.description: The Bay Area Air District issued an air quality advisory until Wednesday as wildfire smoke from Monterey County is expected to drift into the South Bay and East Bay. On Sunday, the Timber Fire started southeast of the unincorporated area of Loma Vista in Monterey County before spreading across several hundred acres. By Tuesday morning, the Timber Fire had grown to 2,000 acres, with only 5% contained. Cal Fire said flames are continuously spreading through grass, brush and oak woodland, forcing authorities to issue multiple evacuation orders and close all state parks in the Big Sur area. On Tuesday, the Bay Area Air District said smoky, hazy skies and the smell of smoke may affect areas in the South and East Bay. The air district said pollution levels were not expected to exceed the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s 24-hour health standards, but the air quality could still become unhealthy as smoke conditions change. The air district said wildfire smoke contains particulate matter and other pollutants that can irritate the eyes and airways, causing coughing or irritated sinuses. Older adults, children and people with respiratory illnesses are especially vulnerable to smoke exposure and should take extra precautions, the agency said. Conditions will continue to be monitored throughout the region and residents can check the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Fire and Smoke Map for air quality levels in their city at fire.airnow.gov. headlines.title: United unveils new nonstop flight from SFO to Trump International Airport
headlines.description: United Airlines will soon offer a weekly nonstop flight from San Francisco International Airport to newly-renamed President Donald J. Trump International Airport in West Palm Beach, Florida. The new service will start in November, with flights only on Saturdays. United is also resuming daily nonstop service between SFO and Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport on Oct. 25. headlines.title: Bay Area radio host Lamont Hollywood laid off from KSAN-FM
headlines.description: Another longtime Bay Area radio host is out of a job as Cumulus Media continues its cutbacks and restructuring. Lamont Hollywood on Monday announced he had been laid off from KSAN-FM, the San Mateo-based rock station 107.7 The Bone. Hollywood most recently hosted “The Lamont Show.” He previously co-hosted the beloved “Lamont and Tonelli” morning show, which aired for more than two decades until 2024. Hollywood’s departure comes after Cumulus laid off broadcast veteran Greg Papa from KNBR last week, citing cutbacks. Papa has been on medical leave as he battles leukemia and other major health issues. Bay Area Aug 6 Music & Musicians Nov 15, 2024 107.7 The Bone's Lamont and Tonelli sign off, ending 35-year run

headlines.title: 2 popular gay bars in San Francisco ‘pause' use of ID verification tech after pushback
headlines.description: Over the weekend, two popular gay bars in San Francisco halted the use of ID verification technology after pushback. Badlands and Toad Hall, both in the Castro neighborhood, opted to pause using Patronscan Guard+, an AI assisted identification reader, similar to what you may see at an airport, after community concerns were raised. Patronscan is an ID scanning technology that can identify fake IDs at a forensic level through comparisons with known fake templates and comparisons with government provided security measures. Servall Data Systems, the makers of Patronscan, also offers a flagging service that can help bars and venues alert their employees of problematic customers and share that information with other establishments that utilize this technology. Opponents are concerned that it is data collection of vulnerable populations and yet another form of tech surveillance in the age of license plate readers and even facial scanning AI. Fight for the Future, an advocacy organization that has been working to prevent AI surveillance technology from being utilized in music venues and bars around the country, called for a boycott all bars in San Francisco that use Patronscan, until they discontinue its use. “We have heard the concerns regarding the use of Patronscan at Badlands and Toad Hall in San Francisco, and we are listening,” said Brian Aranda, director of operations at both bars, in a statement released on Friday. “Effective immediately, we are pausing the use of Patronscan while we review our ID verification and security practices. The safety of our guests and staff remains a priority, as do privacy and trust. Our security teams will continue to thoroughly check IDs manually during this time.” Evan Greer, director of Fight for the Future said that their organization has been working on campaigns to resist AI surveillance since 2019, with a focus on nightclubs and music venues. The push has rallied support from bands like Rage Against the Machine, Bikini Kill, Deerhoof and many others to boycott venues that utilize these types of technologies. Once they learned that several gay bars in San Francisco had adopted the Patronscan technology, their organization setup a boycott petition, both to call for patrons to avoid clubs and bars that use this technology, and to get other bars to state they would never adopt this type of tech at their establishments. So far Greer said that El Rio and DNA Lounge in San Francisco and the La Peña Cultural Center in Berkeley, among others, have signed the pledge. Greer said that this technology won’t actually keep people safe, and that surveillance is typically only used after an act has been committed. “It’s important that we don’t frame this as some kind of philosophical debate between privacy and safety… they’re wasting money that they could be spending on more staff, for example, which actually would lead to more safety in these venues.” said Greer “We’ve all been fed the kind of propaganda stories on TV where we see the, you know, guys in dark suits using technology to track down…that is not how safety happens.” Greer added that their organization’s goal is to slow down the adoption of these technologies while lobbying governments to issue ordinances banning their use. Rhiannon Mosoronchon, vice president of people and operations for Servall Data Systems, said that the company was both aware of the community concerns and the pause in use at Badlands and Toad Hall and said they respected their decision to complete a review as they work through their security practices. Mosoronchon said that while Patronscan does capture a live photo of individuals, it does not utilize facial recognition technology, collect biometric data or use AI in its assessments. While it does store the live photo of patrons on the businesses’ system, those photos cannot be shared, and they are deleted after 21 days in California, in alignment with state law. It does however utilize a forensic-level scan of an individual’s driver’s license to determine if their ID is fake, while providing the door person with additional assistance such as questions to ask to assist with determining if an ID is false. Venues can also flag patrons and share their ID scans and photos on a public flag network, accessible by other venues who use the technology. “We recognize that part of our responsibility is to continue building public trust in and understanding of our system and that this can’t be done through privacy policies or media statements alone – we have to continue holding our team and our venues to the highest standards for transparency, ethical use of our system, and following best practices in privacy and data protection,” said Mosoronchon. Mosoronchon added that patrons at any time can contact the company through their website to request a copy of the data collected and ask for its deletion if they have concerns.

headlines.title: SFMTA launches ‘Fare Day Out' to encourage Muni riders to pay fares
headlines.description: San Francisco transit workers took to Muni buses and trains Tuesday for SFMTA’s first “Fare Day Out,” an effort to encourage riders to pay their fares. Transit workers wearing brightly colored vests and carrying signs traveled along various transit lines to educate riders about fare options and the consequences of not paying. The effort comes as Muni ridership has increased 12% in recent months and fare revenue has surpassed the agency’s projections. SFMTA said fare revenue is $18 million above projections due to growing ridership and increased fare compliance. Despite the additional revenue, the agency continues to face financial challenges. SFMTA is reporting a budget deficit of more than $300 million for the 2026-27 fiscal year. NBC Bay Area’s Ginger Conejero Saab has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Fremont Unified students head back to school
headlines.description: It’s Fremont’s turn to head back to school this week. Students across the Fremont Unified School District headed back to the classroom Tuesday for the first day of the new school year. NBC Bay Area stopped by Ardenwood Elementary School as families arrived for class and students reunited with their classmates. “I’m looking forward to having new friends and meeting a bunch of new people,” one student said. Fremont Unified serves about 33,000 students from transitional kindergarten through high school. The district is also coming off a record year for Advanced Placement exams, with more than 4,600 students passing AP tests last year — the most in district history.

headlines.title: PG&E, East Bay firefighters train for gas line emergencies
headlines.description: PG&E teamed up with East Bay firefighters Tuesday for a safety drill focused on responding to gas line emergencies. The training coincided with National 811 Day, which highlights the hotline people should call before beginning digging projects to help avoid damaging underground utility lines. PG&E said there were more than 500 incidents last year in which homeowners or contractors damaged underground lines while digging.

headlines.title: 3.9-magnitude earthquake shakes Central California, Monterey County
headlines.description: A magnitude 3.9 earthquake struck Central California early Tuesday morning, with the epicenter near Monterey County, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The earthquake occurred at 3:19 a.m. at a depth of about 5 kilometers or 3.1 miles. Its magnitude was initially recorded at 4.0. Its epicenter was recorded at San Benito County, about 3.4 miles southeast of Pinnacles, and around 13 miles southwest of Soledad. No information about potential injuries or damage was immediately released.

headlines.title: Caldecott Tunnel bore to close overnight for maintenance
headlines.description: Caltrans will close Bore No. 3 of the Caldecott Tunnel on westbound State Route 24 on Tuesday night for circuit breaker work and routine maintenance. The closure is scheduled to begin at 10 p.m. The bore is expected to reopen by 4:30 a.m. Wednesday. Caltrans said the same overnight closure will repeat on Wednesday night as crews continue maintenance work.
